chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when children are described as a fitna in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kafi’s chapter on righteousness, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'fitna' here refers to the potential for parental affection to become a spiritual trial if it leads to negligence of divine duties or indulgence in worldly desires. Shia scholars, such as Allama al-Majlisi, emphasize that this does not condemn children themselves but warns against the *excessive* attachment that distracts from God, urging parents to balance love with righteous upbringing (tarbiyah).

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Zareeh,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
en.sarwar: 9. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Dharih who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A child is a trial (mischief, attraction).”’
